requirement: Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST NOT offer a waiver for an uncited first-party Rust function. When a function serves only as an internal implementation detail and no existing requirement explains it, Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST direct agents to propose an explicit project requirement scoped to one area of internal code, such as `internal.config_parsing`, rather than one catch-all requirement, obtain the user's agreement, mark the function with `{impl}`, and run `habeas author --all` for the harness to assess that requirement's evidence. That assessment MUST account for whether the requirement explains each implementing function's behavior. An internal-detail requirement MUST NOT justify an otherwise unspecified end-user-observable behavior.
rationale:
**Verdict: the requirement is satisfied, with one soft spot (see Gaps).**

**What marks the implementation.** The requirement is anchored with `:impl:` on both `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md` and `assets/skills/habeas-bootstrap-requirements/SKILL.md` (`md/requirements/cli.md`). `md/reference.md` only cites it. Skills cannot carry inline references, so file anchors are the intended mechanism. I found no other implementing code.

**Obligation by obligation**
- **No waiver for an uncited function.**
  - The requirements skill says "there is no uncited-function waiver", under "Reviewing code against requirements".
  - The bootstrap skill says "There is no waiver for an uncited function." It also says an enclosing module or `impl` reference does not cover its functions.
- **Propose a requirement scoped to one area, not a catch-all.** Both skills tell agents to propose a requirement "scoped to that area of internal code, such as `internal.config_parsing`, rather than one catch-all".
- **Get the user's agreement.** Both skills say to "get the user's agreement". The requirements skill's workflow section also requires explicit user approval before any requirement is installed.
- **Mark the function with `{impl}`.** Both skills say "mark the helper with `{impl}`".
- **Run `habeas author --all` for the harness to assess that requirement's evidence.**
  - Neither skill repeats this inside the internal-helper sentence.
  - Both skills do give it as the general step for new or changed requirements and forbid the supervising agent from writing evidence itself.
  - The requirements skill says "When a requirement or example changes, run `habeas author --all`". The bootstrap skill has the paragraph "Run `habeas author --all` to create requirement and example evidence" immediately after the internal-helper guidance.
  - The harness-only evidence rule is therefore covered.
- **The assessment must account for whether the requirement explains each implementing function.** The requirements skill says "That requirement's review checks that it explains each implementing function." The bootstrap skill's harness description covers review of the `{impl}` marking. Together they tell agents what the harness will assess.
- **An internal-detail requirement must not justify unspecified end-user-observable behavior.** The requirements skill says "Do not use an internal-detail requirement to justify otherwise unspecified observable behavior." The bootstrap skill says "Do not use an internal-detail requirement to justify unspecified end-user-visible behavior."

**No extra behavior.** The skill text marked `{impl}` for this requirement adds no obligations that conflict with the requirement. The rest of the skill content is covered by sibling requirements (`behavior_review_guidance`, `requirements_review_skill`, `bootstrap_skill`).

**Tests.** No `{test}` reference targets this requirement. The subject is prose guidance in shipped skill files. `tests/symposium_hook_smoke.py` only checks that skills are installed byte-for-byte. A test asserting specific wording would be brittle and add little beyond reading the text. I judge the absence of tests acceptable because the content is simple prose and the file anchors tie the evidence to the exact text, so any edit invalidates it.

**Gaps.** The only soft spot is that `habeas author --all` is not restated in the same sentence as the internal-helper guidance. The general workflow instructions cover it.
